context: a letter from Hermann Kindt, which you are answering
exchanges:
Would you be kind enough to let me know, if it be allowed to translate extracts from your work on “The Contrivances by which Orchids are fertilised by Insects”? A friend of mine in Germany particularly wishes to know this; or if the whole work is in the course of translation? You will know how your writings have captured German students of Natural Philosophy, and how we consider them quasi a commentary to Dr. Louis Büchner philosophical writings. There is a small volume of yours which my friend cannot obtain in Germany; I, therefore beg to ask you, if it was only printed for the Royal Society. The title is: ‘A monograph on the Subclass Cirripedia”.

Allow me to take this opportunity to express to you the admiration I feel for your enlightning writings, and believe me with greatest respect, | Sir, | your obdt servant | Hermann Kindt

Charles Darwin Esq. | M.A., F.R.S., etc.

I am much obliged for your very kind note. I should have been pleased to have given permission for the translation, but my work on Orchids was translated by the late Professor Bronn & published in Stuttgard by E. Schweizerbart. My Monograph on the Cirripedia was originally published by the Ray Society, but can now be purchased at Hardwick’s 192 Piccadilly. It consists of 2 large Vols. with numerous plates & I believe but I am not sure that the price is £1–1–

Pray believe me | Dear Sir yours faithfully | Ch. Darwin
